subject: biology
title: Required practical: effect of antiseptics and antibiotics on bacteria
key_idea: In this practical, discs soaked in antiseptic, antibiotic or plant extract are placed on a plate of bacteria. A clear zone of inhibition forms where the bacteria are killed. The bigger the zone, the more effective the chemical, and a control disc shows the effect of no chemical.

blocks.text: You compare how well different chemicals stop bacteria growing on an agar plate. This section covers the variables, the control and the method.

items.meaning: A chemical that kills bacteria and can be used on skin or surfaces.
A medicine that kills bacteria inside the body.
The clear area around a disc where no bacteria are growing.
A disc with no chemical, used for comparison.

rows: The antiseptic, antibiotic or plant extract (or its concentration)
The size of the clear zone: its radius, diameter or area
A disc soaked in distilled water, or left dry, with no chemical
Species of bacteria, volume and concentration of chemical, size of filter disc, temperature, time, nutrient agar

diagram.alt: Put the steps of the zone of inhibition investigation in the correct order.
steps: Disinfect the work surface and work near a Bunsen flame
Spread bacteria over the agar, lifting the lid only a little
Soak a filter paper disc in each chemical, and one in distilled water
Place the discs on the agar, spaced apart, using sterile forceps
Label the dish and tape the lid on, but not all the way round
Incubate for a set time at a set temperature
Measure the radius or diameter of each clear zone
Calculate the area of each zone using πr² and compare

items: Use aseptic technique: sterile equipment and agar, work near a Bunsen flame and lift the lid only a little.
Use tape to hold the lid on, with a gap so oxygen can enter.
In school, incubate at 25 °C. This prevents the growth of bacteria that are harmful to humans.
Scientists studying bacteria that infect humans may use 37 °C, which is body temperature, where those bacteria grow best.
Soak discs in each chemical and place them on the plate of bacteria.
Include a control disc with no chemical, and control the other variables.
Use aseptic technique and tape the lid on, leaving a gap.

blocks.text: After incubation, look for a clear area around each disc. Bacteria are killed where there is no growth.

items: A clear area means the bacteria have been killed by the chemical.
No clear area means the chemical has no effect, for example if the bacteria are resistant.
The chemical with the largest zone killed the most bacteria.
The control disc should have no clear zone.

blocks.label: Area of a zone of inhibition
where: r is the radius of the clear zone, in mm

items.text: The clear zone for plate B has a radius of 5 mm.

items: Repeat each chemical and calculate a mean.
Use a control disc.
Keep the discs the same size and incubate at the same temperature.
Use more than one type of bacteria.
The test uses only one species of bacteria.
It is done on an agar plate, not on teeth or skin, where the conditions are different.
A chemical used on teeth for only a short time may behave differently.
A bigger clear zone means a more effective chemical.
Area = πr², using the radius.
Repeat and calculate a mean to improve reliability.

checks.q: Why is a disc soaked in distilled water included on the plate?
checks.a: It is a control. It shows the effect of no chemical, and that the results are due to the antiseptic and not the disc.

checks.q: Name two variables that should be controlled in this investigation.
checks.a: Any two from: type of bacteria, volume of chemical, concentration of chemical, incubation temperature, incubation time, size of filter disc.

checks.q: A clear zone has a radius of 4 mm. Calculate its area (π = 3.14).
checks.a: 3.14 × 4² = 50.24 mm², which is 50.2 mm² to 1 decimal place.

exam_phrases: to show the effect of no antibiotics
measure the diameter / radius of each clear area
calculate / measure the area of each clear area
none of the bacteria would be killed (resistant)

mistakes.wrong: The paper disc with no antibiotic is a control variable.
mistakes.right: A control variable is not accepted. The disc acts as a control, for comparison.

mistakes.wrong: The disc with no antibiotic shows the effectiveness of the antibiotic.
mistakes.right: "The effect or effectiveness of the antibiotic" is ignored for the purpose of the control disc. Say it shows that the results are due to the antibiotic, not the disc.

mistakes.wrong: Use πr² to compare the antibiotics.
mistakes.right: "πr²" unqualified is ignored. Measure the radius or diameter of the clear area, then calculate the area.
"Repeat" on its own is ignored. Say repeat and calculate a mean, or repeat and look to see if the results are similar.

worked_example.question: Scientists incubated Salmonella bacteria at 37 °C. Students in school laboratories incubate bacteria at 25 °C. Explain why scientists use 37 °C but students must use 25 °C to incubate bacteria.
answer_points: 25 °C reduces or prevents the growth of bacteria that are harmful to humans.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each point. Say why each temperature is used, not just that one is higher.

exam_phrases: soak a filter disc in each antiseptic
soak a fresh disc in distilled water as a control
place one disc in each quarter / space the discs out
use sticky tape to seal the lid
measure the radius / diameter and calculate the area using πr²
the antiseptic that killed the most bacteria has the largest zone

mistakes.wrong: The test proves that toothpaste kills all bacteria on teeth.
mistakes.right: It does not. It uses only one species of bacteria, it is not done on teeth, and the conditions in the mouth are different.

mistakes.wrong: The clear area around the disc is where the bacteria are growing.
mistakes.right: The clear area has no bacterial growth. The bacteria were killed by the chemical.
Use the radius, which is half the diameter. Using the diameter gives only follow-through marks.

worked_example.question: A student wanted to investigate how effective three different antiseptics were at killing bacteria. The student was provided with an inoculated Petri dish, three different antiseptics, filter paper discs and sticky tape. Devise a plan for the student to complete this investigation. Include a control and any variables that the student would need to consider.
answer_points: Plan: soak one filter disc in each antiseptic, and a fresh disc in distilled water as the control.
Place one disc in each quarter of the dish (spaced out), label the dish and incubate it.
Results: measure the radius or diameter of the clear zone around each disc and calculate the area using πr². The antiseptic with the largest zone killed the most bacteria.
Aseptic and safety: use aseptic technique, work near a Bunsen flame, lift the lid only slightly, and use sticky tape to seal the lid.
Controlled variables: incubation time and temperature, same size of filter disc, same volume of antiseptic, soaked for the same time.
worked_example.tip: Marks are by level. A top answer is a workable plan with aseptic working, a control and at least one variable controlled.

exam_phrases: use sterile forceps to prevent contamination by other microbes
37 °C: any higher and the bacteria might be killed / enzymes denatured
only one plate used / no replicates

mistakes.wrong: Use stronger bacteria, change the time or change the amount.
mistakes.right: "Amount", "stronger bacteria" and "time" are ignored. Say different concentrations or volumes of disinfectant, different concentrations of bacteria, or different types of bacteria.
"Repeat" earns one mark only if nothing else scores. Give a specific change to the method.

mistakes.wrong: Forceps are sterile so germs do not get in.
mistakes.right: "Germs" is not accepted. Say it prevents contamination by other microbes.

worked_example.question: Disinfectants also kill bacteria. Some students do an experiment to see how well four different disinfectants (A, B, C and D) kill bacteria. This is the method they use: mix 2 cm³ of each disinfectant solution with liquid nutrient agar; pour each of the mixtures into separate Petri dishes and allow to set; spread bacteria on the surface of the agar; put each Petri dish in an incubator. One of the students said that disinfectant A is equally effective at killing bacteria as disinfectant B. Explain how the students could improve their experiment to test if that is true.
answer_points: Use different concentrations or volumes of disinfectant (make each disinfectant more dilute).
Use different concentrations or amounts of bacteria.
worked_example.tip: Any two score one mark each. "Amount", "stronger bacteria" and "time" are ignored.
